title: Existence of normalized open scalar compatibility data
statement: For an integral open operation o on j:U→X, there exists ScalarCompatibility l E j o [def-sf-open-tensor-quotient-data], consisting of finite scalar comparisons normalized on every extension-by-zero summand. The strict quotient-tower comparison is supplied separately by ScalarComparison.

source.place: Tags 03DI, 03DA, 0E8I and 0941; identity on extension summands and system assembly.

proof.text: For each n specialize the generic scalar/open comparison [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-adjunction] to the completed coefficient projection on X. Transport it along the continuous pushforward formulas o.integralFunctor and o.finiteFunctor; o.projections supplies the commuting coefficient square. This transport is implemented by the already proved generic private helper openScalarComparison in IntegralOpenScalarRestrictionComparison, not by its consecutive-finite-quotient theorem. Invert the resulting ordinary comparison to obtain finite. Apply its generator formula and cancel the comparison with its inverse to prove sections. Choose these generator-normalized finite comparisons for all n and package the two fields.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03DI, 03DA and 0E8I; specialization of the proved generic open/scalar comparison and cancellation of its generator equation.

statement_change.old_statement: For an integral open operation o on j:U→X, there exists ScalarCompatibility l E j o, including its finite comparison, strict-system comparison, and normalized system evaluation equation.
statement_change.what: Prune the unused independent system comparison and its evaluation field. The old universal evaluation theorem is false: finite and systems are independently chosen isomorphisms, so negating just one gives another permitted choice but reverses its component on a nonzero module (identity open over a point, l=3). The actual scalar-unit and tensor-square proofs use only finite generator-normalized comparisons and ScalarComparison.iso, which already preserves all quotient transitions. Construct the finite normalized comparison directly from the proved generic open/scalar comparison; remove the false unused obligation instead of weakening it or assuming normalization.
